title: Vela Data Systems — LLM architecture & deployment options

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-21 14:30 UTC — duration ~58m. Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SE), Anya (Vela Head of ML), Samir (Platform), Diego (CTO), Ruth (Legal).

00:00:03 Jesse: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick agenda — we want to understand your model needs, constraints, and what success looks like for a pilot.
00:00:12 Anya: Thanks yeah from our side quick context — we run a mixture of analytics pipelines and an internal assistant. Some services will need very long context, up to around 100k tokens for document stitching, others are short chat. Multilingual is important — EN/ES/PT primarily, with occasional FR.
00:00:32 Priya: Got it. When you say 100k tokens, is that peak occasional batches or steady-state?
00:00:38 Anya: Mostly batch jobs that stitch multiple docs per customer, so spikes but predictable. We also want to do tool-calling — e.g., ask for a customer record and call an internal microservice to fetch the latest data.
00:00:50 Samir: And we have strict residency & security requirements — some datasets must stay in our VPC or on-prem. We need KMS integration and audit logs for every inference.
00:01:03 Marco: Perfect, we support multiple deployment patterns that map to that. For the private option we can provision a VPC/private control plane and integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management. Audit logs and RBAC we can expose via the console.
00:01:16 Diego: From the CTO perspective latency matters for the assistant — sub-200ms token latency ideally — but for the doc stitching batch jobs we care more about throughput and total cost. So there's a tradeoff.
00:01:28 Priya: Right, we typically recommend routing latency-critical traffic to lower-context, lower-latency model variants and batching the long-context jobs perhaps on dedicated pools with higher memory/quantization profiles.
00:01:42 Anya: How flexible is Redwood on model selection? We prefer open models but need them tuned for instruction following and some fine-tuning. Also tool-calling — we need deterministic JSON outputs.
00:01:53 Jesse: We have a model catalog with curated open models and verified performance profiles. For very long context we recommend models with efficient attention and/or retrieval + KV caching. We can also provide quantized variants for Dedicated to reduce cost.
00:02:10 Samir: A question on KV cache — is that the same as prefix caching? Sometimes I hear kv cash in other calls and I'm never sure.
00:02:17 Priya: (laughs) KV cache, yes — key-value cache, helps with streaming and prefix reuse. In our runtime we do continuous batching and KV cache management to speed up subsequent completions when you have repeated context. It reduces compute for repeated tokens.
00:02:31 Anya: For 100k token context, are we talking models like longformer variants or retrieval augmented? What's Redwood's approach?
00:02:40 Marco: Two levers — model architecture and system-level tricks. We support models with extended context (some open models now support >64k), and for very large contexts we recommend combining retrieval + chunking and a lightweight aggregator model to keep token costs down. Another approach is to use a streaming prefix store and only send the deltas.
00:02:59 Diego: Okay, concrete question: can we host this in a VPC, have KMS, and still use Redwood's managed control plane? We prefer the control plane to be customer-managed for sensitive stuff.
00:03:10 Jesse: Yes, we offer a Private deployment where you can run the control plane in your account or a customer-managed VPC; we also have an on-prem package for air-gapped needs. In that mode you retain key custody and we can integrate with your KMS/HSM.
00:03:23 Ruth: From legal — we need SOC 2 type II and audit reporting. What evidence do you provide for data residency and retention?
00:03:30 Jesse: We have SOC 2 and tenant-level audit logs. I will share the security pack; Priya will include a note on what is available in Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted.
00:03:40 Anya: On multilingual — we do machine translation fallback in some flows, but prefer models that natively handle multi-lingual understanding and code-switching. Any bench for ES/PT?
00:03:52 Priya: We run multilingual evals and can share benchmark sheets. For Portuguese especially, model quality varies; sometimes it's better to fine-tune or use a separate regional model. We'll include BLEU/ROUGE style metrics and human eval samples in the benchmark plan.
00:04:06 Samir: Tool-calling reliability is critical; we need strong guarantees around schema adherence and error handling. Can Redwood do function calling or structured output enforcement?
00:04:18 Marco: Yes, we support structured output and function/tool calling primitives. Our SDKs include typed function schemas and post-call validation. That said, no model is 100% deterministic — we'll propose a wrapper that validates outputs and triggers fallback logic for mis-formed responses.
00:04:33 Anya: Any notes on cost? We're sensitive — long-context jobs can balloon token costs.
00:04:38 Jesse: We typically show cost tradeoffs via unit economics — model size, tokens in vs generated, quantization. For Dedicated you can often reduce cost by using quantized variants and reserved GPU capacity; for Hosted you get simplicity but per-token costs are higher. We'll send examples based on your expected token distribution.
00:04:55 Diego: For throughput, do you support autoscaling and burst capacity?
00:04:59 Marco: Yes, Dedicated pools have configurable autoscaling and burst options. Private deployments can include autoscaling depending on your infra config.
00:05:07 Ruth: One compliance detail — can you restrict data retention for specific models or endpoints? We need to ensure certain data is never logged.
00:05:14 Priya: You can set per-route retention policies and disable logging for sensitive routes in Private/Dedicated. Hosted also supports retention controls but for the highest assurance you should use Private with customer-managed keys.
00:05:28 Anya: For the benchmark, what do you need from us?
00:05:31 Priya: Sample prompt set, a few representative workloads (assistant short chat, long doc stitch, multilingual examples), and desired SLOs for latency/cost/quality. We'll propose a test harness and instrumentation so you can reproduce results.
00:05:45 Samir: Do you support on-prem GPUs like A100s and also AMD variants?
00:05:51 Marco: Yes, runtime supports nvidia and some AMD stacks; we'll include a hardware compatibility matrix.
00:05:57 Anya: Are there existing customers doing 100k token stitching?
00:06:01 Jesse: A few enterprise customers use long-context pipelines combining retrieval; we'll anonymize case studies and include relevant perf numbers in our follow up.
00:06:10 Diego: Can we get a canary / A/B rollout plan? We want to start small with non-critical data then expand.
00:06:15 Marco: Absolutely — rollouts, canaries, A/B, and automatic fallback policies are supported.
00:06:22 Ruth: Please include contract language about liability and data handling.
00:06:25 Jesse: Will do, legal pack in the follow-up.
00:06:30 (brief cross-talk)
00:06:40 Priya: Quick note — for the 100k token test we'll likely recommend retrieval + a 32k+ context model for the aggregator, instead of sending 100k tokens into one pass, depends on your latency budget.
00:06:55 Anya: That makes sense. Would be great to see a couple concrete config examples.
00:06:59 Jesse: We'll provide a few blueprint configs: Hosted small-scale, Dedicated reserve with quantized large context, and Private on-prem with customer KMS.
00:07:08 Samir: About tool calling — can the calls go through a service mesh or do we need direct egress?
00:07:14 Marco: You can route tool-calls through your internal service mesh; for Private we can deploy connectors inside your VPC to avoid public egress.
00:07:22 Diego: Any performance regressions we should be aware of with quantization on long context?
00:07:28 Priya: There can be small quality regressions for certain tasks; our Optimize tool recommends quantization profiles per workload and will flag quality regressions tied to prompt evals.
00:07:38 Anya: Great. Let's recap next steps.
00:07:41 Jesse: Recap: we'll send pricing + SLA + security pack, Priya will share benchmark plan and example prompts, Marco will send private deployment checklist and hardware matrix. Vela to share sample prompts and confirm pilot scope.
00:07:55 Ruth: We'll review legal pack and come back with contract questions.
00:08:00 Diego: Schedule the benchmark kickoff for the week of Sep 1st, preferably Sep 2nd morning PST.
00:08:07 Jesse: Sounds good — we'll follow up with a calendar invite. Thanks everyone.
00:08:12 (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had minor errors (KV cache -> KV cash in one segment, VPC sometimes spelled V-P-C).
